placements.why: The e2e suite asserting a concrete behavioral rule (save-triggers-reviewer-enrollment) is an organizational-strategy-grade concern about how the system's structural behavior is defined and guaranteed — no existing strata category covers this, and it is the kind of top-level organizational bucket (system design/behavior guarantees) that future envelopes about the product's architecture would keep feeding.
placements.title: system behavior is codified as enforceable rules, not just described
placements.frame: What behavioral guarantee does this rule encode into the system, and how is it kept verified as the system evolves?

placements.title: saving a memory silently confers reviewer authority on its creator
placements.frame: What governance role does the act of saving a memory confer on its creator, and how does the e2e suite keep that rule enforced as the system changes?
placements.why: src-1 states the rule itself (saving a memory enrolls the creator as reviewer) as an operational fact the e2e suite enforces; src-2 frames the probe memory's entire existence as carrying that assertion. Together they name a recurring subject — an automatic role-enrollment rule tied to an action, verified by test infrastructure — that future envelopes about reviewer assignment, permissions, or e2e coverage of governance rules would keep feeding, not a one-time fact. No existing leaf or strata (both empty for this repo) plausibly held this theme, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Architecture strata as the closest organizational home for a system-behavior rule.
